provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: count the 4-connected components of the snake colour (the walls) and emit a strip of background colour whose length is (wall count + 1). The generator guarantees this equals the number of background regions the walls cut the canvas into. The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. The snake colour is the constant palette[5] and the background fill is the constant palette[0]. 4-connectivity is unchanged by every D4 transform, so the count needs no rewriting. The output is an (n+1)x1 column in canonical coordinates. Reversing each row of a one-wide column leaves it unchanged. An odd number of clockwise rotations (d4%4 in {1,3}) turns it into a 1x(n+1) row, and an even number keeps it a column. The factory therefore specializes only the strip orientation and the two colour constants. Ties and objects at the boundary don't matter: walls touching any edge are still counted as single components, and rectangular grids are handled generically.
draft_notes.limitations: The program relies on palette[5] being the only non-background colour, which holds across the constructor's domain (only colours 0 and 5 appear). It counts wall components rather than separately computing background regions. The constructor rejects samples where these two counts differ, so they agree on all generated data. I found no contradiction between the fixtures and the uniform rule. One thing for host review: the constructor's bounded fallback (one straight wall at column 1 on a canvas that defaults to 3x3) still produces a valid two-row output, so it is not a defect in the rule.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Count the 4-connected components of the wall colour (palette[5]). Emit a one-wide strip of background colour (palette[0]) of length n+1. The strip is a column when d4%4 is even and a row when d4%4 is odd. The constructor makes the label len(snakes)+1 and rejects any sample where the wall-component count is not len(snakes) or the background-region count is not len(snakes)+1. So the wall-count reading and the region-count reading agree on every emitted pair.
evidence: The label `output = common.grid(1, n + 1, BG)` with `n = len(snakes)` is fully determined by the visible input. The guard `_components(flat) != len(cand)` ensures the number of constructed snakes equals the visible 4-component count of colour 5. No hidden latent leaks into the label.

The region guard `_components(empty) != len(cand) + 1` handles two lane cases. A winding snake in a lane of width 2 or more can carve extra background pockets beside it. A snake hugging both canvas edges can leave fewer regions. Both cases are rejected, so both interpretations hold on all emitted data.

The majority guard `(w*h - len(flat))*4 < len(flat)*5 -> continue` keeps background at least 1.25 times the wall cells. This makes the factory's constant BG consistent with the archived program's `background()` choice of most common colour.

`_sample_lanes` cannot produce zero-width lanes. Since n <= span//3, the minimum total of widths plus gaps is 2n-1, which is less than span, so the reduction loop stops before any width reaches 0. Lanes are separated by at least one empty column or row, and the component check also enforces this independently.

`_sample_snake` places a contiguous horizontal run on each shift row and then continues from nx, so each snake is internally 4-connected. Each row's cells are unique, so the duplicate check only matters across snakes.
The horizontal orientation maps sampler coordinates (r in [0,w-1], c in a lane of [0,h-1]) to (c, r), which is a valid in-bounds transpose.

The factory solver reads the augmented grid directly with the colour constants WALL=palette[5] and BG=palette[0]. It uses 4-connectivity, which is invariant under D4. It specializes only the strip orientation, and odd quarter-turns map a column to a row while flips leave a one-wide column a column. There is no whole-grid untransform/solve/retransform wrapper.
The validate() fixtures give component counts 2, 1, 4, 3 and 2, producing outputs of height 3, 2, 5, 4 and 3, which matches the approved fixtures.
Host audit: passed, with 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants and no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The synthetic distribution is narrower than the originals. All snakes are lane-parallel and span the canvas edge to edge in one orientation per grid. The originals include corner-to-edge snakes (e.g. train 3's snake at (6,9)-(8,9) running to the right and bottom edges) and mixed orientations. This is a scope restriction, not a labelling error.
The snake count is capped at 6, so outputs have length at most 7.

The bounded fallback (one straight wall at column 1) is practically unreachable within 200 tries, and its label is consistent: two regions, output length 2. If a caller passes width < 2 the fallback would index out of range, but the documented domain is 3..30.
The solver assumes palette[5] is the only non-background colour. This holds because the constructor emits only colours 0 and 5.
required_context_checks: Confirm the host D4 convention is that d4%4 counts quarter-turns, with indices 4-7 adding a reflection, so that odd d4%4 is exactly when the canonical column becomes a row. The host audit passing over the augmented checks supports this.

No colour-association evidence check is needed. e872b94a is not in the episode-evidence list, and the rule involves no arbitrary colour or shape lookup. Output orientation is a deterministic consequence of D4 and is taught by every demonstration's output shape.

host_review.resolution: Source and audit agree. Generator remains narrower than original fixtures: lane-parallel snakes and maximum six walls. Record this limitation for subsequent diversity work; do not claim it covers every arrangement.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
